correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 34–63 for a type-one seed and column-parent means. With f=R_u/R_0, det(aI−M)=−uD and the smaller eigenvalue is below a; the larger is Perron, including u=1 by nonnegative irreducibility (the proof's wording 'positive matrix' is imprecise at u=1). The positive Perron amplitude gives the advertised tail sign when D≠0. The derivative of f has at most one zero since it is a sum of two distinct real exponentials. In the B=0 case Cayley–Hamilton gives f''(0)=uD; for D=0 the trajectory is constant or a constant plus one decaying exponential. These facts cover all strict, zero, and competing signs and give the unique crossing when claimed. Inverting I−M under D<0 gives the excess sign b(1−a+c)−a(1−d); crossing the positive endpoints of the interval for b gives c<a−d exactly. The integrated difference rises and then falls strictly to that resolvent excess, including strict finite-time positivity in the zero-limit case. Lifetime integration equals expected progeny by Tonelli and the mean-one lifetime of each newborn. Replayed the printed rational witness by direct determinant/resolvent algebra and independently bisected f−1 on [1,15], obtaining 6.658067198520774. Inspected checker.py and VERIFICATION.md without executing them; finite tests are illustrative, not the classification proof.

value.rationale: Separates three naturally competing quantities—initial activity, asymptotic reproduction, and cumulative volume—in a motivated two-channel model. The sharp intensity-independent wedge and finite-horizon sign law, including a nonzero transient excess at equality of total means, are more informative than a single engineered example. Value is mathematical and does not establish effects of a real platform policy.
